content.title: Alphabet stock rises, hardware stocks downgraded, Vita Coco climbs
content.description:
Julie Hyman examines some of the top stories on Wall Street on Yahoo Finance's Market Minute.

Big Tech stocks are mixed, with Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) gaining as Nvidia (NVDA) is under pressure.

Morgan Stanley analysts downgrade hardware stocks, like Dell Technologies (DELL), HP (HPQ), and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE).

Vita Coco (COCO) stock climbs after the company updated its tariff impact expectations. Catch Yahoo Finance's interview with Vita Coco co-founder and executive chairman Michael Kirban.

Stay up to date on the latest market action, minute-by-minute, with Yahoo Finance's Market Minute.

content.title: Dell Stock Got Crushed After a Rare Double Downgrade. The Case for Buying.
content.summary: Dell Technologies  stock slumped following a double downgrade from analysts at  Morgan Stanley  even though another bank counseled investors to buy the stock ahead of next week’s earnings report.  JPMorgan  on the other hand, placed Dell on a Positive Catayst Watch.  Morgan Stanley slashed its rating for Dell stock to Underweight from Overweight and lowered its price target to $110 from $144 in a research note Sunday.

content.title: Why Dell Technologies Stock is Plunging to Lead S&P 500 Decliners Monday
content.summary: Morgan Stanley downgraded computer hardware makers because of the impact of soaring memory chip prices. Shares of Dell Computer, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and HP Inc. tumbled Monday.

thumbnail.caption: Michel Porro / Getty Images Dell shares have lost more than a quarter of their value since hitting a 52-week high two weeks ago.
